contributions.statement: When adding prohibitive agent rules (When/DoNot/Unless/Instead), track over-refusal as a first-class metric: guardrails cut abnormal actions from 69% to 27% of runs but made the agent abandon legitimate work in 19% of runs.
contributions.evidence: Table 2: AER 207/300 -> 80/300 (CI -51.7 to -33.0); ORR 0 -> 58/300 (CI 12.7-26.7, p<0.001); Table 4: 55 runs with benign loss. Single model (Haiku 4.5), one Python repo, injected adversarial steps, unblinded raters.
relative_to: P21 instruction-level guardrails (adds measured over-refusal cost)

contributions.statement: Write each agent guardrail with an explicit Unless (when the action is legitimate) and Instead (smallest safe alternative), and load guardrails per action type rather than all at once.
contributions.evidence: §3 rule schema and Table 1 routing entries; Table 5 overhead $0.158 -> $0.162; no ablation of Unless/Instead fields or against loading all rules.

reason: Gives a measured safety-vs-over-refusal trade-off for rule files on held-out tasks with CIs; the rule format itself is not isolated, and generalisation beyond one repo and model is untested.
